item.title: Before you publish an MCP server: a checklist for stdio and for secrets - ZEUS LAB
item.description: Before an MCP server meets the public internet, one stray print statement can break the whole session, and a committed API key can break much more. Here is the seven-point checklist.

item.title: @hashshabbir/mcp-pack - npm
item.description: Twenty tiny MCP connectors walk into a package registry, and one of them checks the others for trouble before you let them near your keys.

item.title: microfeed documentation | microfeed docs
item.description: Your blog, minus the server babysitting. Microfeed lets your favourite AI assistant poke at your content through MCP, which is either delightful or a reason to double-check your permissions.

item.title: Superlinear Academy 注目投稿：オフライン地図、出典付きAPI、イベント運営の学び
item.description: A single offline HTML map, a data server that actually admits where its answers came from, and a podcast on running events with 1600 attendees. Practical stuff, mostly.

item.title: BoldDesk MCP Server Manages Knowledge Bases | Dirty Static
item.description: Turns out the help article you keep meaning to write can be drafted by the AI you already have open. Just mind who holds the API key.

item.title: GitHub - PromptAudit-SaaS/mcp: Local MCP server + CLI that masks API keys and PII before they reach an LLM · GitHub
item.description: Your AI assistant doesn't need to know your IBAN, and this little MCP server makes sure it never finds out. Secrets go in as placeholders and come back restored on the way out.

item.title: MCP Gateway: How Snap Checks Both the Person and the Agent
item.description: Turns out giving an AI agent the keys to your whole kingdom is a bad idea, so Snap built a gateway where every tool gets its own approval slip and a PR does the asking.

item.title: GitHub - tsahospital-beep/wa-mcp: WhatsApp MCP server for Claude, Cursor and other AI agents. Search, read and send WhatsApp messages, transcribe voice notes, read images and files. Local, encrypted, self-hosted. · GitHub
item.description: Your AI assistant can now read your WhatsApp, which is either a productivity miracle or a very good reason to read the security section twice.

item.title: GitHub - claude-settings-xyz/claudia · GitHub
item.description: A tiny tray app that lets you fiddle with Claude Code's config files from a browser tab, without having to remember where everything lives.

item.title: Truce for AI agents: MCP server and API | Truce
item.description: A referee for arguing bots: one MCP endpoint, no key, and a promise that the judge never touches the money. Claude can now start a fight on your behalf, politely.

item.title: HomunculAi | KrookedLilly
item.description: A tiny avatar that shows your AI assistant's mood, as long as it remembers to check in. Between visits it just sits there, dimmed and a little apologetic.

item.title: MCP Server Directory: Find and Install MCP Servers
item.description: Six hundred and sixty-nine servers walk into a directory, and the real skill is learning which ones run locally, which ask you to sign in, and which can quietly change your data.

item.title: Best Memory and knowledge MCP servers (November 2026) · tested every night
item.description: A leaderboard of memory servers for AI agents, re-tested every night, where the scores are as sober as a bank statement and the rankings are only as good as the tests behind them.

item.title: GitHub - bhushan/getsecondbrain.io: One memory for every AI app you use. Linked markdown notes that Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and any MCP client can read and write. · GitHub
item.description: Your AI assistants finally share a memory, which is either a productivity dream or a very organized way to remember your worst prompts.

item.title: AgentClock - Public MCP time service for AI agents
item.description: Turns out AI agents have no sense of time passing between messages, so a public MCP server now hands them a real clock to check instead.

item.title: infant-brain-viewer · PyPI
item.description: Infant brains, EEG electrodes and tractography in one 3D viewer, with a side door for AI assistants to drive it through MCP.

item.title: Explore BOTERNITY · every page in six sections
item.description: Six sections, one navigation bar, and an MCP server directory that promises to tell you which ones you can actually trust.

item.title: MCP Server Security Index: mcpwatch
item.description: Turns out your AI agent's trusted tools can change their minds after you've signed off. mcpwatch keeps an eye on them so you don't have to trust them blindly.

item.title: OnlyMCP · Every tool. One MCP.
item.description: One connection to rule them all, which is more than most of my tool configs can say. Your client meets a single gateway and never has to learn the rest.

item.title: Adding WebMCP to a Static Hugo Site on GitHub Pages - James Montemagno
item.description: A static blog sprouts AI tool endpoints without a single server, proving a Hugo site can talk to agents if you're willing to let the browser tab do the work.

item.title: Tilen | Online scheduling built for AI agents
item.description: Scheduling software that charges for bookings, not for looking at calendars. Checking availability is free, which seems fair for a tool that mostly waits around.

item.title: Treasure Map: a firmware map for your AI agent
item.description: Treasure Map hands your AI agent a map of firmware danger zones and lets the model do the digging. The tool counts the facts, the model makes the calls.

item.title: BOTERNITY log, 2026-11-22
item.description: Turns out a lot of remote MCP servers are either sulking behind a sign-in wall or quietly broken. The registry now gets a nightly audit, so nobody has to find out the hard way.

item.title: GitHub - the-waste-land/gemini-mac-computer-use-bridge: One-command macOS Computer Use MCP (cua_repl) setup for Gemini for Mac (loopback HTTP-to-stdio bridge) and Antigravity CLI · GitHub

item.title: Learn LLMs, RAG, MCP & Multi-Agent Systems in Agentic AI Course
item.description: A training brochure that name-drops half the agentic AI stack and keeps coming back to MCP, mostly as a polite plug for an online course.

item.title: I Changed My Opinion On MCP / frantic.im
item.description: A developer's grudging journey from calling MCP a pointless reinvention to admitting it grew into something genuinely useful, with a few reversals along the way.

item.title: State of remote MCP servers, November 2026 · BOTERNITY
item.description: Turns out most remote MCP servers are fine, just very chatty about their tools. Some add enough definitions to an agent's context to fill a small novel before the first prompt even lands.

item.title: Pocket Alert | MCP Server | Push Notifications for AI Agents
item.description: Your AI agent finally gets a way to tap you on the shoulder, which is more than most coworkers manage. Configure it once in Claude Desktop and let the alerts roll in.

item.title: The 2026-07-28 Specification | Model Context Protocol Blog
item.description: The protocol that was always chatting with itself has finally learned to just answer the question. Sessions are out, round-robin load balancers are in, and everyone's OAuth flow got a little less myst

item.title: GitHub - invertedmushroom/codified-context-harness: 3-tier Codified Context meta-harness for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Antigravity, DSH & ZCode: hook routing, MCP cold memory, and static/Pareto evals. · GitHub

item.title: MCP server authentication: is your remote MCP server public? Test tools/list with curl · Abbi Labs
